key_insight: GRAC proposes combining graph-based representations of surgical scenes with retrieval-augmented captioning to generate scene descriptions informed by recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge.
problem_solved: Understanding surgical activities for documentation, training, performance assessment, and workflow review often requires time-consuming manual review and clinical expertise.
method: Represent surgical scenes as graphs to structure scene information.
Use retrieval augmentation to incorporate relevant prior knowledge into caption generation.
Generate surgical scene descriptions; the truncated abstract does not provide implementation details or evaluation results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, GRAC suggests a way to combine structured scene representations with retrieval for specialized captioning. It could reduce manual surgical review, but the supplied abstract does not establish performance or clinical benefit.
visual_elements: Surgical scene thumbnail beside a simplified graph of scene entities and relationships.
Pipeline diagram: surgical scene → graph representation → knowledge retrieval → generated caption.
Illustrative retrieval panel linking a current scene to related surgical activities.
Application icons for documentation, training, performance assessment, and workflow review.
paper_title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
paper_authors: Rochak Dhakal, Chen Zhao, Soup Cobb, Xin Qian, Xiaofeng Yang
